# PREFIX-706-R6 — Asymmetric Bernstein/BRC corner rectangles: 12.25× larger certified exclusion

Date: 2026-11-11 (Asia/Shanghai).
Frozen scientific input: awdawmip/enterprise-math@f42f2906d77f24085c123f3ccfe9667d41caa96d (unchanged).
Parent objective: PREFIX-675, global maximum of the frozen two-stream statistical observer on the complete auxiliary square D=[0,1/2]^2.
Direct dependencies: PREFIX-621/622 exact stopped-clock observer; PREFIX-700 original 189-level integer survivor recurrence and moment kernel; PREFIX-705 exhaustive Bernstein certificate of monotone survivor tails and Efron–Stein corner boxes.
Research origin: independent BRC observer-optimization unit, not a shared-task CLAIM; previously observed R6 research activity RA-0AA45C8056A76CE3060E2C23 is provenance, not an authorization token.
Status: AUTHOR_RECOMPUTED / EXACT_FRACTION_IMPLICATION_CHECKED / UNREVIEWED / NOT_ADMITTED.

## Precise problem and BRC carrier

The original two labelled independent first-stop signed-information branch populations remain unmodified. Let N_p in {25,...,189} be the number of informative signs until stopping, and let s_n(p)=Pr(N_p>n) for 0<=n<=188. Given N_p=k, the completion time T_p is gamma(k,1). For independent streams, Y(p,z)=max(T_p,T_z), mu=E[Y], W=Var(Y). Define V_q(p,z)=q² W(p,z)-q mu(p,z), q real >=2, and f_t=W-t mu, t=1/q in (0,1/2]. The argument also permits t=0 as a mathematical limit.

The square (p,z) is an auxiliary probability-parameter observer space, not a native X6 spatial plane. Full labelled branch multiplicities are retained through s_n and the exact clock kernels; the proof uses only the declared moment observer and is not a claim about native heartbeat evolution.

PREFIX-705 proved with 17,766 exact Bernstein derivative-coefficient signs that every s_n is nondecreasing on [0,1/2]. It also proved the tensorized variance inequality W(p,z)<=Var(T_p)+Var(T_z) and found the exact comparator e=(0,3/20).

## Theorem 706.1 — General two-width corner-rectangle criterion

For 0<a,b<1/2 with a+b<1/2, define low interval I_L=[0,a] and high interval I_H=[1/2-b,1/2]. Let C(a,b) be the union of the four closed product rectangles I_L×I_L, I_L×I_H, I_H×I_L and I_H×I_H. Put

L(a)=sum_{n=0}^{188}(2n+1)s_n(a)-600,

U(b)=189+sum_{n=0}^{188}(2(189-n)-1)[1-s_n(1/2-b)],

B=W(e)-mu(e)/2.

Then for all real q>=2 and every x in C(a,b),

V_q(e)-V_q(x) >= q² [B-max{2L(a), L(a)+U(b), 2U(b)}].

Whenever the right bracket is positive, all of C(a,b) is rigorously excluded from the set of global maximizers, and the total area of these disjoint rectangles is (a+b)².

Proof. For a Poissonized gamma clock, Var(T_p)=E[N_p]+Var(N_p). Since E[N_p]>=25, E[N_p]-(E[N_p])²<=-600, giving Var(T_p)<=E[N_p²]-600=L(p), with E[N_p²]=sum(2n+1)s_n(p). Stochastic monotonicity of all tails gives L(p)<=L(a) for p in I_L. Writing D_p=189-N_p, Var(T_p)<=189+E[D_p²], and E[D_p²]=sum(2(189-n)-1)(1-s_n(p)), which is nonincreasing in p, so Var(T_p)<=U(b) on I_H. Apply the Efron–Stein tensorized variance inequality to Y=max(T_p,T_z) to obtain the three listed upper bounds for W over the four rectangles. Since mu>=0, f_t(x)<=W(x), and f_t(e)=W(e)-t mu(e)>=B for 0<=t<=1/2. Subtract and multiply by q². The product rectangles are pairwise disjoint because a+b<1/2, giving area a²+2ab+b². QED.

## Theorem 706.2 — An 11.62-fold enlargement with the original 9.3q² margin

Take a=1/64, b=1/11. The checker executes the frozen 189-level survivor recurrence and the exact rational witness moments. It certifies the following strict upper bounds from full fractions (the millionth-tick brackets are in the accompanying JSON):

L(1/64) < 275220941/1000000,
U(1/11) < 271896052/1000000,
B > 559812917/1000000.

Thus max{2L,L+U,2U}<550441882/1000000. For every real q>=2 and every x in C(1/64,1/11),

V_q(e)-V_q(x) > (9371035/1000000) q² > (93/10) q².

The excluded exact area is (1/64+1/11)²=5625/495616, or 5625/484 times the original PREFIX-705 four squares (area 1/1024). Numerically this is more than 11.62 times the previous excluded area, while retaining the strict 9.3q² margin.

## Theorem 706.3 — A 12.25-fold enlargement with a positive uniform margin

Take a=1/64, b=3/32. Exact rational results:

U(3/32) < 279763527/1000000,

and the largest of the three clock-variance upper bounds is 2U < 559527054/1000000. Therefore for every real q>=2 and every x in C(1/64,3/32),

V_q(e)-V_q(x) > (285863/1000000)q² > (7/25)q² >0.

The excluded total area is (1/64+3/32)²=49/4096. Relative to PREFIX-705 this is exactly (49/4096)/(1/1024)=49/4=12.25 times the original area; relative to the full square's area 1/4 it excludes 49/1024 (approximately 4.785%) of parameter space uniformly in all real q>=2.

These two rectangles give different useful tradeoffs: 706.2 preserves a larger certified comparison margin, while 706.3 removes more of the parameter domain. They are full continua, not finite parameter samples.

## Verification and reproducibility

Source file: PREFIX706_R6_ASYMMETRIC_CORNER_RECTS.py. It calls the already published PREFIX700_R6_STRICT_OPTIMIZER_ORDER.py and recomputes all 9,529 nonzero survivor cells, the three exact variance bounds, the comparator's exact mean and variance, exact rational gap bounds and both areas. It checks the precise integer millionth-tick enclosures and strict margins; no floating-point decisions are used.

Author local execution of an equivalent original frozen recurrence and the new exact checker: ALL_CHECKS_PASS PREFIX706-R6. The original PREFIX-705 complete Bernstein derivative-sign certificate is reused at its original statement and not rerun here. No original full-domain CAD, independent referee check, native X6 heartbeat update, or global optimizer-location solution is asserted.

Method reuse: PREFIX700 original recurrence/moment kernel (REUSE_EXECUTED in equivalent local code); PREFIX705 positive survivor-tail order and Efron–Stein contract (REUSE_APPLIED). Observed moment compression is valid only for this declared V_q objective and the presented variance upper bound; it is not a quotient of signed path provenance for arbitrary subsequent BRC operations.

## Unfinished scientific frontier

The excluded regions are now asymmetric: the high-bias tails contribute much larger safe intervals than the low-bias tails. The exact next discriminating problem is to determine, for all real 12<=q<=24, whether rational Bernstein bounds on 2D interior cells can certify fixed-witness or piecewise-witness domination, extending exclusion beyond the four corners. Use the complete finite survivor population and compare f_t at both endpoints t=1/24 and 1/12 when the witness is fixed; the difference is affine in t, so positive endpoint certificates imply continuum coverage. Preserve positive-dimensional stationary components and the still-open PREFIX-675 interior/global-maximizer problem.
